summary: Weekend spike: unexpected embedding usage charges and invoice overage
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaDocs reports higher-than-expected charges for embedding requests executed during a weekend batch window (2026-03-07 22:00 UTC to 2026-03-08 05:00 UTC). The spike appears limited to embedding endpoints and correlates to a synchronised batch job their side runs nightly.

Impact:
- NovaDocs observed a ~3.1x increase in billed embedding units compared to their expected usage for the weekend billing period.
- This resulted in an overage charge on invoice INV-2026-03-08 which the customer disputes.
- Customer is self-serve; high sensitivity to cost — requests credit/adjustment and confirmation that future runs will be metered correctly.

Environment:
- Customer production account (acct_id: cust_00C2X)
- Region: us-east-1
- Endpoints: /v1/embeddings (model redwood-open-embed-v2)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger nightly batch of 1.2M small docs (avg 36 tokens) via retry logic using exponential backoff across 20 workers starting 2026-03-07 22:00 UTC.
2) Observe normal success rates but increased per-minute request rate spikes at worker restart windows.
3) Compare billed embedding units in Console > Billing > Usage for the timeframe with application-side counters.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows 3.1x reported embedding units billed between 2026-03-07 22:00 and 2026-03-08 05:00 UTC.
- Customer-side application logs show no corresponding increase in completed requests recorded.
- Retry bursts observed in application logs at worker restarts; some requests returned HTTP 5xx followed by retries.

Expected behavior:
- Billed units should align with successful requests and our retry deduplication rules; transient 5xx retries should not double-bill when identical request IDs are provided.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer provided aggregated application counters and samplings of request IDs (attached in ticket file list).
- Billing export CSV for 2026-03-07 to 2026-03-09 (attached).
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Kapoor: Created ticket after receiving customer escalation via support@. Customer requests immediate credit and short explanation of cause.

2026-03-10 Ethan Morales: Acknowledged. Assigned to billing + metering for priority triage. Asked customer for sample request IDs and exact invoice line items to validate. SLA commitment: initial response within 24 hours.

2026-03-11 Billing Team (Marta Liu): We see an unusual increase in embedding units in the billing export for cust_00C2X. Raw meter shows a spike starting 2026-03-07 21:57 UTC. Opening INT-412 to correlate internal metering pipeline health during the window.

2026-03-11 Customer (NovaDocs - Alex Chen): Provided sample request IDs and confirmed client used stable idempotency keys for retry logic. Also attached app logs showing retries with HTTP 503 responses from API gateway.

2026-03-12 SRE (Diego Ramos): Noted increased 502/503 errors in api-gateway autoscaling window (22:00-23:00 UTC). Possible partial duplicates due to proxy-level retries not propagating idempotency key header. Adding instrumentation trace links.

2026-03-13 Ethan Morales: Interim update to customer: we will provisionally credit the disputed overage while investigation continues and share reconciliation details. Credit will appear as CR-7321 on next invoice unless root cause requires sustained adjustment.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Hypothesis A - Metering double-count due to proxy-level retries lacking idempotency headers; api-gateway returned 5xx to client but forwarded duplicate requests to serving-runtime which were counted as billable attempts.

2026-03-11: Hypothesis B - Upstream client retried without idempotency and server accepted multiple requests; customer claims they used idempotency keys, so we need to verify header preservation through our gateway and any load balancers.

2026-03-12: Billing export analysis: billing raw_meter shows 1.9M embedding units billed in the window vs customer app counters of ~600k completed requests. Pattern matches multiple entries for same request_id in meter log.

2026-03-12: Traced sample request_id abc123.. through gateway logs: initial request from customer had header 'Idempotency-Key: nd-req-457' but subsequent forwarded requests from our api-gateway to backend lost the header in two of three cases due to a middleware bug introduced in release 2026-03-05 (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/commit/5e1b9f6).

2026-03-12: Confirmed serving-runtime counts billable units at time of request ingestion (not final success). Therefore duplicate forwarded requests without idempotency keys are billed separately even if dedup later would have suppressed responses.
2026-03-12: Correlated with INT-412 where autoscaler restarted a subset of gateways causing transient worker restarts and replays. Root cause points to header drop during replay path.
resolution: 2026-03-13: Short-term remediation: Issued provisional credit to NovaDocs for the disputed amount (billing credit CR-7321 equal to $14,752). Credit applied to account cust_00C2X and will appear on next invoice. Customer notified.

2026-03-13: Engineering fix: Reverted middleware change introduced 2026-03-05 and deployed a patch to preserve idempotency headers during proxy retries (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/283). Hotfix deployed to us-east at 2026-03-13 03:20 UTC.

2026-03-13: Billing adjustments: Backfilled meter reconciliation for affected window; duplicate meter entries for request IDs with missing idempotency keys were collapsed in offline reconciliation job and billing export regenerated. Confirmed final billed units align within 2% of customer counters after reconciliation.

2026-03-13: Follow-ups: Create automated alert for embedding unit delta > 25% between separate meter exports (real-time vs. offline reconcile) and add end-to-end idempotency propagation tests to CI to prevent regressions. Assigned to INT-415 for production tests and documentation updates.
2026-03-13: Customer acceptance: NovaDocs accepted provisional credit and requested a follow-up walk-through of mitigation steps; scheduled a call on 2026-03-16.
